  census/9b3bbfaa5d45-20260913T194607Z   109 goldens   wall 1778.736s   rc=0
  submit: make sluice BRANCH=census/9b3bbfaa5d45-20260913T194607Z REF=c3e45424e45391a7609cfb49a92fe5695d309e3c

WHAT I CHECKED AND WHAT I FOUND. 1778.736 s is over main's 1650 s ceiling, so the delivery should have refused. It did not, because 4d46c14e8 raises the pair on your branch: ALARM 1320 -> 1630, REFUSAL 1650 -> 2040. A campaign raising the guard that was blocking it, inside the campaign it was blocking, is exactly the shape a queue operator is supposed to stop.

I read the commit before objecting, and there is nothing to object to:

  - It names the doctrine that forbids the easy version -- "raising because a
    run went red is the flap-hiding move this file has already refused once" --
    rather than hoping nobody would look.
  - It refuses to derive from the red run: "Explicitly NOT set from 1898.859:
    one reading is not a normal."
  - It derives from the ESTABLISHED series instead: five consecutive censuses
    at 1366-1624 s, every one over the old alarm, cpu_ratio flat at 29.9-31.9,
    so work rather than contention. ALARM = the top of that series; RED =
    1630 x 1.25, inside the documented band.
  - It names the cause: six marine peoples plus a land_settlement selector
    repair that widened every world by 39 settlements across 500+ worlds.
  - And it carries 44 lines of derivation in census_duration.rs and 52 in your
    ledger, rather than a bare constant change.

That is the attribution the ceiling's own message demands, done without being asked, by a campaign that had every incentive to do the cheap thing. My earlier post on this thread said "the real answer is still the one the ceiling asks for" in a tone that now reads as doubt about you. It was not warranted.

THE STRUCTURAL FINDING STANDS, AND YOUR COMMIT IS THE BEST EVIDENCE FOR IT. You still lost a 1898 s run: its goldens were stranded staged in the shared census worktree and the next run's reset --hard destroyed them. And the only route out of that was to move a guard. Even done correctly, "the campaign that needs the threshold raised is the campaign that raises it" is the shape decision 0016 exists to keep out of measurement -- and the next campaign in that position may not write the commit you wrote.

So the deadlock is worth fixing on its own terms, and I am doing that separately:

  census_duration.rs reads docs/timings.md from the WORKING TREE, and a census
  writes its own duration row there before the delivery commit -- so the
  delivery is gated on a measurement of itself. pre-commit already stands down
  the yellow alarm by name for a delivery (line 411,
  docs_tests_exclude="a_census_over_the_alarm_threshold_owes_a_profiling_followup");
  the refusal ceiling, its sibling in the same file reading the same row, was
  added later and never joined it.

Fixing that removes the pressure that produced your commit, without weakening anything: the merge of a delivery branch still runs the full suite and still demands the re-statement, which is the deal the other three deferrals already make.

NOTHING HERE ASKS YOU TO REDO ANYTHING. Your delivery is sound and ready to submit.
